prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map orders the indoor scene into clear depth layers: in the foreground (roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres away, within the camera wearer's and opponent's arm's reach), a vertical perforated Connect Four game board sits at the bottom center and rises into view from frame 1 to frame 4, while the camera wearer's own left arm and hand holding a red token enter from the bottom left in frame 5 as the brightest, nearest surface (~0.2 to 0.4 metres away). Directly behind the board (roughly 0.9 to 1.3 metres from the camera wearer and 0.3 to 0.5 metres behind the board), a woman wearing dark glasses and a puffy jacket sits on a couch facing forward and looking downward toward the board between them, with the couch cushions extending behind her to the left and right at roughly 1.2 to 1.8 metres and a floor lamp at the far right edge at ~2.0 metres. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint pitches downward and moves slightly closer to the table from frames 1 to 4 before tilting slightly back in frame 5, while the seated woman leans forward in frame 3 to extend her right hand over the top of the board (~0.6 metres from the camera) to drop a yellow token, then lowers her arm to her right side in frame 4 and leans back into the couch in frame 5 as the camera wearer's left arm reaches up and partially occludes her right side. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the metric separation between the foreground board, the woman's reaching hand, the couch cushions, and the recessed background walls (which drop off into dark values beyond 3 to 5 metres) immediately apparent, and it even resolves the depth through several circular holes of the game grid. However, the depth map is unreliable Inside some of the small circular cutouts of the Connect Four board—where background depth bleeds inconsistently with the foreground plastic—and along the distant ceiling grid and recessed hallway, which are compressed into a nearly uniform black region.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the primary foreground actors and furniture against an unlabelled background: the seated woman in front of the camera wearer (~0.9 to 1.3 metres away, facing the camera and looking down at the game) is segmented as a 'person' across all five frames, flanked left and right by the sofa cushions behind her (~1.2 to 1.8 metres away) labelled as 'couch' from frame 2 onward, while the Connect Four board at the bottom center (~0.5 to 0.7 metres away, within arm's reach of both people) is segmented in frames 3 to 5. In frame 5, the camera wearer's reaching left forearm and hand (~0.2 to 0.4 metres away on the lower left) are segmented as a second 'person' instance that overlaps and partially occludes the couch on the left and the seated woman's right arm behind the board. Across the 5-frame sequence, the segmented 'person' mask of the woman shifts higher in the frame and expands to the left in frames 3 and 4 as she leans forward and extends her right arm over and then beside the board, while the board mask at the bottom grows larger from frame 3 to 4 as the camera tilts down. While segmentation sharply delineates the outer silhouette of the reaching arms, torso, and furniture boundaries that blend into the busy office background in RGB, it suffers from severe semantic and boundary errors. Specifically, it misclassifies the vertical open-front zipper and collar gap of the woman's jacket as a 'tie' in every frame, mislabels the blue Connect Four grid as a 'laptop' in frames 3 to 5 (missing it entirely in frames 1 and 2), splits the sofa cushions into multiple 'couch' and 'bed' instances, and completely omits the yellow and red game tokens, ceiling, walls, and floor lamp.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks the 2D keypoints of the woman seated roughly 0.9 to 1.3 metres in front of the camera wearer: across all five frames, a cluster of yellow facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) shows her head centered and facing toward the camera wearer while angled slightly downward toward the game area below. In frames 1 and 2, only her head keypoints and a nearly horizontal yellow line connecting her left and right shoulders are detected, as her lower torso and arms are occluded or cropped at the bottom of the frame behind the game board. In frame 3, as she leans forward within arm's reach of the board (~0.6 metres from the camera), her full upper-body trapezoid (shoulders and hips), left arm, and raised right arm appear in yellow alongside a dense cluster of magenta right-hand keypoints positioned just above the left side of the board where she holds the yellow token. In frame 4, the skeleton captures her right arm extending downward and to the image-left as her magenta right hand drops to waist level beside the couch cushion, while in frame 5 her torso shifts back and a magenta hand skeleton reappears near her right shoulder. This map makes her head orientation, shoulder tilt, and right-arm trajectory explicit without visual clutter, but it is highly unreliable in frame 5, where it fails to assign a separate body skeleton to the camera wearer and instead fuses the camera wearer's foreground left hand (~0.3 metres away) onto the distant woman's right arm and hand keypoints (~1.1 metres away), while also missing her torso in frames 1 and 2 and her left hand throughout.
